\section{Reproducibility, nonclaims, and open problems}
\label{qua:sec:scope}

The standard-library script
\path{experiments/quantum_ramsey/implicit_majority_audit.py} is invoked by
\begin{verbatim}
python3 experiments/quantum_ramsey/implicit_majority_audit.py \
  --self-check --max-k 12 --simulate-k 3 --trials 20
\end{verbatim}
It verifies the dyadic error schedule, prefix-product inequality, and variable
recurrence with exact rational arithmetic through $K=64$.  It also compares
the size-biased survival lemma with an exact dynamic program over all split
trees through nine levels, emits the Jain-et-al./Liu--Zhandry exponent
translation, checks conditional marked-item uniformity by an explicit
16-dimensional Grover state-vector calculation, and runs deterministic-seed
diagnostics on complete, empty, parity, and random graphs.

The end-to-end graph diagnostic replaces quantum search by an ideal uniform
marked-item sampler; only the isolated capped-search primitive receives the
small state-vector check just described.  These checks test the combinatorial
invariant, error schedule, and sampler symmetry.  They are not hardware
results or empirical proofs of quantum speedup.  The theorem is the analytic
argument in
\cref{qua:sec:model,qua:sec:algorithm,qua:sec:correctness,qua:sec:complexity}.

The positive theorem uses no topological subroutine.  Separate Hodge and
reconfiguration routes were examined: single-edge recolouring graphs are
hypercube subgraphs, while homological encodings either inherit expensive
state preparation or hide the original search in a top-dimensional simplex.
Those observations are stop rules for the current topology route, not
lower bounds against every future topological quantum algorithm.

Three open problems delimit the contribution.  First, resolve the discrepancy
with the printed Jain--Li--Robere--Xun quantum lower bound.  Second, determine
whether a randomized classical algorithm can match the
$\widetilde O(\sqrt M)$ upper bound; \cref{qua:prop:classical-lower} leaves a
large exponent gap.  Third, determine whether the implicit-set method can be
adapted to off-diagonal or hypergraph Ramsey total search, and whether the
multicolour bound in \cref{qua:cor:multicolour} can be sharpened by a scale-aware
estimator.

No numerical Ramsey bound, $R(3,18)$ witness, physical speedup, or
quantum-versus-all-classical separation follows from this part.
